about: States with a statewide recall law whose signature requirement is tiered, ranged or compound, so no single threshold is read. Each row says why and cites the corpus row (data/municipal-elections/92O-national-state-baseline.json, secondary-synthesis-only). Read by src/core2/gov-rules/municipal-election-rule-packs.ts.

CA.why: Tiered by registered voters: 30% under 1,000; 25% for 1,000 to 10,000; 20% for 10,000 to 50,000; 15% for 50,000 to 100,000; 10% for 100,000 and over.
CA.citation: Cal. Const. art. II sec. 19; Cal. Elec. Code div. 11 (sec. 11000 et seq.)

DC.why: Compound: 10% of registered electors District-wide plus 10% of registered electors in at least 5 of the 8 wards.
DC.citation: D.C. Code sec. 1-204.111 et seq., sec. 1-1001.16

FL.why: Two petitions: 10% of registered electors (7.5% in cities over 25,000, 5% over 100,000), then a second petition of 15% more within 60 days.
FL.citation: Fla. Stat. sec. 100.361 (Uniform Municipal Recall Statute)

LA.why: Tiered by registered voters: 40% under 1,000; 33.3% for 1,000 to 25,000; 25% for 25,000 to 50,000; 20% at 50,000 and over.
LA.citation: La. Const. art. X sec. 26; La. R.S. 18:1300.1 et seq.

MT.why: Tiered by city size: 15% for cities over 1,000, 20% for smaller.
MT.citation: Mont. Const. art. XI sec. 8; Mont. Code Ann. title 2, ch. 16, pt. 6

WA.why: Tiered by city class (25% for first and second class, 35% for others) of votes cast for the office, after a mandatory court sufficiency hearing.
WA.citation: Wash. Const. art. I secs. 33, 34; RCW 29A.56.110 et seq.
